nodes.name: Robust and efficient visual odometry using colored point cloud maps via dual-sparsity and hierarchical optimization
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable localization is fundamental to navigation in GNSS-challenged environments, yet monocular visual odometry (VO) inevitably suffers from drift without global constraints. Point cloud maps can provide global corrections to mitigate this drift. However, existing heterogeneous feature registration methods fail to fully exploit the shared information between vision and point clouds. This limitation results in suboptimal localization accuracy, reduced robustness, and increased computational overhead. To address these issues, we propose a visual odometry system based on colored point cloud maps, which leverages both the global point cloud map as a constraint and the shared modality (color) between the colored point cloud map and the camera to ensure localization accuracy and robustness. The system consists of two main components: sparse colored point cloud construction and visual localization. In the sparse colored point cloud construction module, we introduce a map sparsification strategy that associates visual gradients with point clouds, ensuring that the retained sparse point cloud preserves salient visual gradient information, thereby reducing computational costs. This strategy is further incorporated into the vision-to-map matching stage, forming a “dual-sparsity matching” scheme. In the localization stage, we propose a hierarchical optimization-based iterative Kalman filtering algorithm, which performs multi-level iterative optimization over multi-resolution images to prevent localization from getting trapped in local optima while enhancing accuracy. Experiments on public and self-collected sequences demonstrate significant gains in both accuracy and efficiency. Compared with a representative map-based method (DSL), the proposed approach reduces ATE (RMSE) by $$52\%$$ 52 % – $$95\%$$ 95 % across multiple challenging sequences, with a representative improvement from 1.883 to $$0.152\,\text {m}$$ 0.152 m on R3live_5 ( $$91.92\%$$ 91.92 % reduction). Against the learning-based I2D-Loc++, our method achieves accuracy gains of up to $$76.6\%$$ 76.6 % and maintains robust tracking in extreme cases (e.g., R3live_3/4 ) where I2D-Loc++ and ORB-SLAM3 fail due to visual degradation. Furthermore, the system maintains near real-time efficiency, reducing total processing time by up to $$47.7\%$$ 47.7 % (e.g., from 121.11 to $$63.34\,\text {s}$$ 63.34 s on Whu_1 ). Even under severe geometric degeneracy, our tracker remains robust with an ATE of $$0.076\,\text {m}$$ 0.076 m , whereas geometry-only LiDAR–IMU localization degrades to $$9.23\,\text {m}$$ 9.23 m .

nodes.name: Enhancing sparse multi-view super-resolution with unified multi-plane image spatial representation
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract The popularization of multi-camera systems and multi-view image capture has led to the emergence of sparse multi-view image super-resolution (MVSR) as a promising research direction. The primary approach to sparse multi-view super-resolution (SR) currently involves extending traditional single-view SR and stereo SR frameworks, i.e., extracting features from each view and performing pixel-domain alignment and fusion to leverage cross-view reference information. However, this straightforward framework has two main drawbacks. First, performing cross-view fusion in the pixel domain disregards the spatial perception information that multi-view images provide. Second, feature alignment and fusion across views introduce considerable redundant and repetitive computations, which hinders further scalability to more viewpoints. This paper proposes a novel sparse multi-view SR framework based on a unified spatial representation reference. Specifically, the proposed method first computes a multi-plane image spatial representation from the multi-view images. This multi-plane image (MPI) representation encapsulates all the information from each view and has spatial perception. Subsequently, an upsampled reference image is rendered from the MPI representation for the low-resolution views. A high-low frequency separation fusion network is then proposed to upscale the input low-resolution images based on the rendered reference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for recovering high-frequency details.

nodes.name: Polarimetric image restoration with adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization-based color correction
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Optical electronic devices often exhibit certain limitations when attempting to capture underwater images, such as poor contrast, color casts, and blurry details. To improve the image quality of underwater scenes, polarization-based methods are introduced to enhance the underwater image. Nevertheless, the enhancement performance of most current methods is limited by their manual backscatter region selection processes and their disregard for color and brightness restoration. In this paper, we propose an underwater polarimetric image restoration method based on adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization (AoP)-driven color correction. Specifically, we construct an adaptive standard deviation of Gaussian filter-based on the entropy of the input image to capture the complete backscatter light. Afterward, we correct the color casts based on a reference channel and two gain coefficients, fully considering the color attenuation introduced by the difference in the AoP, and simultaneously utilize the AoP map and the gray-world assumption to spatially modulate the correction process. Finally, we comprehensively consider the brightness information of HSV and normalized backscatter light estimation to design an adaptive gamma revision function, thus naturally adjusting the enhancement results. The enhancement results on the underwater polarimetric image dataset show that our method achieves a good enhancement ability with high contrast, reasonable appearance, and natural brightness. Moreover, the extensive histogram distribution and image segmentation experiments demonstrate that our enhancement results have almost the same histogram distribution for the r, g, and b channels and can yield more accurate segmentation effects.

nodes.name: Efficient Residual Learning With Multi-scale Attention for Robust Coal-rock Image Classification
nodes.abstract: Abstract Robust coal-rock image classification is challenging because visual differences among coal, gangue, limestone and sandstone are often subtle and can be obscured by lighting variation, dust, humidity, sensor noise and complex texture similarity in mining environments. This study proposes an efficient multi-scale attention residual learning framework for image classification, aiming to improve the balance among classification accuracy, parameter efficiency, convergence speed and cross-domain robustness. The proposed network introduces a residual convolutional block that integrates efficient multi-scale attention for spatial and channel-wise feature enhancement, while replacing conventional convolutions with depthwise over-parameterised convolution during training to improve convergence without increasing inference complexity. The model is evaluated on three public natural image benchmarks, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and CINIC-10, and on a proprietary four-class coal-rock dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks while maintaining a moderate parameter scale. On CIFAR-100, it improves classification accuracy over several attention-enhanced residual baselines, and on COALSet-4 it obtains a substantial improvement compared with the corresponding residual baseline, indicating stronger adaptability to fine-grained industrial visual patterns. Ablation experiments further suggest that both the multi-scale attention component and the modified convolutional operation contribute to accuracy gains and faster convergence. Visual inspection of attention regions indicates that the model can focus on discriminative local texture structures. The results demonstrate the potential of efficient multi-scale residual learning for coal-rock recognition and related industrial image classification tasks. Our source code is available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20841285}{10.5281/zenodo.20841285.

nodes.name: Computational text indicators of epistemic norms in higher education: auditable cross-validated prediction against a weak observed household-resource baseline
nodes.venue: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study tests whether computational text indicators of epistemic norms add out-of-sample predictive value for normalized academic results beyond a weak baseline of directly observed household/resource indicators. Design/methodology/approach Data comprise 263 students observed in two waves across five sites. Prediction uses 263 follow-up records. The baseline contains seven observed indicators. Archived epistemic counts were generated through pre-assigned mappings for closed items and LDA/topic-model-assisted processing for open responses. A deterministic 10-fold split (seed 60126) evaluated raw counts, within-fold PCA, and fixed outcome-independent ENA coordinates using pooled OOF R2, RMSE and MAE. Findings No epistemic specification reliably improved the baseline. Pooled OOF R2 was −0.009 (M0), −0.065 (M1), −0.032 (M1-PCA) and −0.008 (M2). M1 significantly worsened MAE after Holm correction; H1 and H2 were not supported. Research limitations/implications The baseline is weak, no prior-achievement variable is available, corpus-level reliability of automated epistemic variables is unknown, ENA coordinates were fixed before resampling, and program representation is imbalanced. Practical implications The indicators should not be used for high-stakes decisions without prospective measurement, subgroup-fairness and instructional-utility validation. Originality/value The study provides an auditable reporting object linking feature provenance, leakage risk, resampling controls and reporting requirements, and shows why null or adverse predictive results should be retained.

nodes.name: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
An Artificial Intelligence Framework to Predict Box Office Performance through Multimodal Analysis of Movie Trailers and Online Audience Responses
nodes.venue: International Journal on Artificial Intelligence Tools
nodes.abstract: In the film industry, box office predictions are crucial for making investment decisions, marketing plans, and distribution choices. Current prediction approaches mainly use movie metadata or single-modal information, ignoring trailer video content and audience responses, resulting in low prediction accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework is novel in that it uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM)–Attention (CNN–BiLSTM–Attention) regression and Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO)-based feature selection to integrate trailer visual features, trailer audio features, movie metadata, and audience responses into a single multimodal architecture. The proposed framework used the Movies YouTube Trailers and Sentiment dataset, which was preprocessed using mean value imputation, followed by Min–Max normalization and one-hot encoding. Vision Transformer (ViT) was used to extract visual characteristics from the trailer, and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), chroma, spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, and Root Mean Square (RMS) energy were used to extract audio features. Audience response features were derived from sentiment scores, favorability, and vote counts. Visual, audio, metadata, and audience response features were fused into a unified multimodal representation. In order to forecast box office revenue, ARO chose the CNN–BiLSTM–Attention network’s most informative feature subset. Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0246, Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0009, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.0304, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.0586, and Coefficient of Determination [Formula: see text] of 0.9549 were all attained by the suggested model. The results showed that the proposed model improved prediction accuracy and provided an effective decision-support tool for movie producers and distributors.

nodes.name: International Journal on Artificial Intelligence Tools
THE EMPLOYEE TRAINING BUSINESS PROCESS IN AN IT COMPANY: DIAGNOSING THE CURRENT MODEL AND LEVELS OF MANAGERIAL DECISION DELEGATION TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
nodes.venue: State and Regions. Series: Economics and Business
nodes.abstract: The article examines the employee training business process of an IT company as an object of process management under the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI). The purpose of the study is to formalise and diagnose the current model of the training process, to establish its systemic limitations, and to develop a classification of AI functions by the level of delegated managerial decision. The methodological basis comprises the process approach, systems analysis, functional decomposition, lean waste analysis and expert estimation. A process passport is compiled in a diagnostic format, an AS-IS flowchart is constructed as a linear sequence of nine stages, and a quantitative decomposition is performed: the full cycle lasts 9–12 months, while the share of stages that add value directly to the employee does not exceed 15–20 %. Waiting and unused employee potential are shown to be the dominant categories of waste, and the open-loop character of the control circuit is identified as the key systemic limitation. Four root causes of inefficiency are established, and it is demonstrated that they form a closed causal loop reproducing itself irrespective of the quality of learning content. The scientific novelty consists in the formalisation of the training process passport through the category of the competence gap, and in a classification of artificial intelligence functions by the level of delegated managerial decision (L0–L4) whose criterion is not the technical sophistication of the model but the scope of authority transferred to the algorithm; a normative rule is justified prohibiting the delegation of decisions with personnel consequences above level L2. Practical value: the process passport, the waste map, the list of root causes and the delegation scale constitute a diagnostic toolkit suitable for auditing the learning and development function and for designing an artificial intelligence usage policy in human resource management. It is advisable to direct further research toward verifying the current-state model and designing an improved process model capable of eliminating the identified cause-and-effect loop.

nodes.name: State and Regions. Series: Economics and Business
SegRef3D Lite: A browser-based workflow for artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation and quantitative three-dimensional morphological analysis
nodes.abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

nodes.name: Research on a Bayesian Estimation Image Reconstruction Method for Geiger Mode Avalanche Photodiode Light Detection and Ranging (GM‐APD LiDAR) Based on Spatiotemporal Features of Sequence Data
nodes.abstract: In scenes with strong background light, three-dimensional LiDAR imaging still faces problems such as incomplete imaging and residual background noise. This paper proposes a Bayesian-estimation image reconstruction method based on sequence data. Sparse range-intensity sequence data are constructed, and the signal probability and average intensity features of the sequence data are fused to build the likelihood term, thereby highlighting the differences between signal and noise. Through spatiotemporal average-intensity gradient analysis, the MRF prior parameters are adaptively estimated, and a spatial-continuity prior with edge-preserving characteristics is constructed. Under the Bayesian maximum a posteriori estimation framework, spatiotemporal feature fusion is transformed into an energy-minimization problem. The iterative conditional modes algorithm is then used to solve the optimal range image with spatial average intensity as a constraint, and morphological filtering is used to remove isolated noise points. With a data volume of 20,000 frames, the recovery ratio of the reconstructed range image in the 730 m scene reached 82.6%. In the 2,000 m long-range scene with an extremely low signal-to-background ratio (SBR), the recovery ratio reached 56.3%, representing a 46.2% improvement over the SPIRAL method, with an RMSE of 1.77 m. Partial reconstruction can also be achieved in low-SBR regions of long-range buildings, improving target completeness under low signal-to-background ratio conditions.

nodes.name: Next-Generation Cybersecurity for Quantum-Safe Satellite Data:Post-Quantum Cryptographic Framework and Advanced Algorithms
nodes.venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
nodes.abstract: Conventional cryptographic mechanisms in satellite communication systems are facing great challenges due to the swift progress of quantum computing. Current methods like RSA are quantum vulnerable and there is a pressing need for quantum secure cybersecurity. In this study, the authors suggest a new cyber security framework for secure satellite data transmission with the help of the post-quantum cryptographic methods and intelligent cyber threat detection mechanisms. The proposed approach consists of the following three components: (1) quantum-resistant key generation and encryption using CRYSTALS-Kyber, (2) authentication of digital signatures using CRYSTALS-Dilithium, and (3) an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a Deep Neural Network (DNN) designed for detecting cyberattacks in real time. An additional Quantum Resistance Score (QRS) model also is integrated to assess security robustness against quantum threats. Experimental results show that Kyber obtains efficient encryption and decryption times of 22 μs and 30 μs, respectively, while the size of the ciphertext is compact, at 1,088 bytes. The DNN model attained 98.7% accuracy, 98.2% precision, 97.9% recall, and 98.0% F1-score. The framework resulted in a 96% QRS, attack detection rates of more than 96.9% and throughput of 95 Mbps. The results show that the framework can securely, efficiently and quantum resistively protect next-generation satellite communication systems.

nodes.name: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
NeuroTürkNet: A Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Brain MRI Tumor Classification and Localization
nodes.abstract: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) presents challenges for computational tumor classification and localization because tumor appearance and surrounding anatomy vary across examinations. This work presents NeuroTürkNet, a two-stage prototype that combines a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) for four-category image classification with a YOLOv8n model for tumor-region localization. Input MRI images were resized to 640 × 640 pixels and processed using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) and bilateral filtering. The classification dataset comprised 3,264 publicly sourced images, and the localization dataset comprised 5,858 annotated images. The CNN was trained with Adam optimization, class weighting, and validation-based learning-rate scheduling; the YOLOv8n component was trained separately and applied to images classified as tumor-bearing. In the detailed test results reported for the classifier, accuracy was 90.84%, precision 90.87%, recall 90.84%, F1-score 90.80%, and ROC-AUC approximately 0.99. The localization component reported an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.81, a best mAP@50 of 0.88, and best precision of 0.85. A graphical prototype supports MRI upload, visualization of predicted regions, and PDF output. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed computational workflow on the datasets described, but they do not establish clinical diagnostic validity. Independent validation and a complete audit of dataset partitions are needed before medical deployment.

nodes.name: Multimodal biomarkers of Parkinson’s disease risk in essential tremor. (A prospective cohort study)
nodes.venue: S.S. Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry
nodes.abstract: Objective. To identify clinical and neuroimaging biomarkers associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD) onset in patients with essential tremor plus (ET-plus) during prospective observation. Material and methods. This prospective observational cohort study included 159 patients diagnosed with essential tremor (ET), ET-plus, ET-PD, and idiopathic PD. The median observation period was 4.6 years. All participants underwent standardized neurological examinations and assessments, including the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale Part III (UPDRS-III), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), Unified Dystonia Rating Scale (UDRS), Fahn-Tolosa-Marin Tremor Rating Scale, Non-Motor Symptoms Scale (NMSS), olfactory testing, screening for probable REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), Stroop test, forward and backward counting tests, Boston Naming Test, literal and semantic verbal fluency tests, transcranial sonography (TCS) of the substantia nigra, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with nigrosome-1 assessment. Results. Conversion from ET-plus to PD occurred in 15 patients. The most significant predictors of conversion were hyperechogenicity of the substantia nigra on transcranial Doppler (TCD), absence of nigrosome-1 on MRI, probable REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and ET duration greater than 20 years. The predictive model demonstrated high discriminatory power (C-statistic 0.89). Clinically, patients who converted showed a combination of non-motor symptoms, cognitive decline, signs of nigrostriatal dysfunction, and more frequent resting tremor. Conclusions. The risk of Parkinson’s disease onset in patients with ET-plus is determined by a combination of multimodal biomarkers. The prospective identification of 15 patients who converted supports classifying this subgroup as a high-risk phenotype that warrants ongoing monitoring and comprehensive evaluation.

nodes.name: S.S. Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry
Multimodal Accessibility and Spatial Equity of Public Activity Facilities for Children and Adolescents in Wuhan, China: Implications for Socially Sustainable Urban Planning
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Background: Equitable access to public activity facilities for children and adolescents is an important dimension of social sustainability and sustainable urban mobility, yet evaluations based on static distance or a single travel mode may misrepresent service opportunities. Methods: Using Wuhan as a case study, we constructed 600 stratified community demand points representing approximately 1.90 million residents aged 5–19 years and evaluated 180 facilities. Baidu Maps navigation times for walking, weekday after-school door-to-door public transit, and driving were incorporated into a truncated Gaussian two-step floating catchment area model. Population-weighted coverage, inequality, spatial clustering, and supply–demand mismatch were assessed, with sensitivity tests for supply weights, age composition, demand definition, and route-time uncertainty. Results: Within 30 min, population-weighted coverage was 37.85% for walking, 28.44% for public transit, and 94.20% for driving. Wider time thresholds reduced weighted Gini coefficients but did not eliminate positive spatial clustering. Under the 60 min public-transit scenario, four peripheral districts contained 78.00% of the high-demand–low-service proxy population; their combined share remained 80.34% when demand was defined by population density, although classification of individual units changed. Accessibility rankings were stable under supply-weight and age-group sensitivity tests, while repeated driving observations revealed threshold-crossing uncertainty. Conclusions: Broad driving coverage cannot substitute for neighborhood-scale walking and public-transit opportunities. The framework provides an auditable tool for monitoring the spatial inclusiveness of public services and identifying priorities for facility infill and first/last-mile improvements, thereby supporting socially sustainable urban planning. The results represent potential service opportunities rather than actual travel behavior, facility use, or a comprehensive assessment of social equity.

nodes.name: Lightweight tomato disease recognition in complex environments based on improved YOLOv8
nodes.venue: PeerJ Computer Science
nodes.abstract: With the continuous expansion of tomato cultivation, early identification and accurate control of diseases are crucial for reducing economic losses and ensuring food security. However, in natural scenarios such as greenhouses and fields, challenges like complex backgrounds, drastic lighting changes, and limited computing power of edge devices make it difficult to achieve both high accuracy and real-time detection. To address these issues, this article proposes a lightweight real-time detection method based on an improved YOLOv8 and constructs a hybrid scenario dataset, TomatoDataset, for validation. The dataset includes samples from complex field environments and controlled settings to ensure the visibility of fine-grained characteristics of tiny disease spots. Methodologically, a lightweight backbone utilizing Inverted Residual Blocks and Depthwise Separable Convolutions is designed to significantly compress the parameter space while preserving feature expression capabilities. Furthermore, a Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism is embedded in the feature fusion stage to enhance directional perception, and the Scale–Sensitive Intersection over Union (SIoU) loss function is introduced to optimize bounding box regression for tiny targets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an F1-score of 74.65%, mean average precision (mAP)@0.5 of 79.5%, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 41.6% on the TomatoDataset. On the NVIDIA Jetson Nano platform, the per-image inference latency is only 33.6 ms. Compared with the mainstream lightweight model YOLOv8n, our model reduces the parameter volume by 46.9% while improving the F1-score by 1.9%. This study achieves a coordinated optimization of detection accuracy and computational efficiency, providing a viable solution for real-time tomato disease monitoring on edge devices.

nodes.name: Leakage-aware multimodal GeoAI for residential rent valuation: evidence from Arabic property listings in four Saudi cities
nodes.abstract: Abstract Automated valuation models (AVMs) increasingly combine structured property attributes with listing text and location, yet their reported accuracy depends on how the data are cleaned and partitioned. This study evaluates a multimodal GeoAI workflow for annual villa rents in Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Al-Khobar using public Aqar listings that pair structured attributes with Arabic descriptions. Listings were linked to a national district gazetteer (98.5% of the analysis sample matched), from which district centroids, district area, distance to the city centre and an inverse-distance spatial lag of neighbouring district rents were derived. A data audit showed that 2,197 of the 3,718 published records (59.1%) were exact duplicates, rising to 86–92% in Dammam and Al-Khobar. Gradient boosting with structured, text and geospatial inputs was compared with hedonic and random-forest baselines under four validation designs. With duplicates retained, random cross-validation gave a median absolute percentage error (MdAPE) of 1.5% and an R² of 0.82 on log rent; after de-duplication these became 15.4% and 0.60, and under district-grouped validation 19.3% and 0.55. Under district-grouped validation, geospatial context reduced mean absolute error by 20.6% (95% district-bootstrap interval 14.6–26.1%) relative to structured attributes alone and removed significant residual autocorrelation in Riyadh (Moran’s I from 0.40 to − 0.01). Text reduced error by 6.2% on its own but added no significant gain once geospatial context was present. Split-conformal intervals reached 91.6% coverage at the nominal 90% level, while leave-one-city-out transfer degraded all models (MdAPE 26–34%). De-duplication and spatially grouped validation should accompany reported AVM accuracy.

nodes.name: Large-extent Classification of Wetland and Management Types Using Satellite Remote Sensing and Auxiliary Data
nodes.venue: Mires and Peat
nodes.abstract: There have been few studies examining how effectively land use / land cover (LULC) classes of wetland types and their management can be detected with remote sensing and auxiliary data. We conduct wetland-specific present-day LULC classification and long-term change detection in seven European study areas. We assess how accurately LULC types and their changes can be detected with satellite remote sensing and to what extent auxiliary data improves classification accuracy. We conduct 10 m spatial resolution 27-class LULC classifications using Sentinel-1 and -2 satellite imagery and auxiliary GIS data about soil, LULC, and topography. For the change detection, we distinguish 8 LULC classes between 1985 – 2023 using Landsat imagery at a 30-meter resolution. The classification accuracy for the present-day analysis varies between 52–93 %, with the omission of auxiliary datasets reducing accuracy by up to 41 %-points. The change detection classifications have 73–94 % agreement with the Corine Land Cover data. Our results indicate that wetland and management types can be classified using 10-meter imagery, but the use of good quality auxiliary data is required to improve the classification accuracies. Additionally, 30-meter LULC changes are detectable using Landsat imagery. The developed approach allows for quick and straightforward implementation of LULC classification and change detection over large areas.

nodes.name: Instance-Specific Brain Image Registration: Learning Deformable Fields from a Single Image Pair without External Datasets
nodes.venue: Physics in Medicine & Biology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objective: To eliminate the reliance on large-scale external training datasets and achieve high-precision alignment for complex brain structures by overcoming the prevalent challenges of data scarcity and domain shifts in current deep learning-based registration methods.Approach: We propose a novel Instance-Specific Deep Brain Registration Framework that independently trains a dedicated model for each specific image pair. By reconceptualizing a single image pair as an internal dataset generator, we introduce a Multi-Scale Random Patch Learning strategy to construct a diverse local-to-global sample space. Architecturally, we design a Context-Aware Flow Predictor integrated with a Recurrent Context Transfer mechanism within a coarse-to-fine paradigm. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Adaptive Optimization strategy is incorporated during the inference phase. By dynamically tracking the local spatial folding status, it adaptively adjusts spatial regularization to effectively suppress topological distortions while maximizing voxel-level accuracy.Main results: Extensive experiments on mono-modal, multi-modal, and pathological brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our method can handle large anatomical deformations without relying on external training datasets. It achieves highly competitive registration performance compared to mainstream population-based and implicit neural representation methods. Crucially, it balances this alignment precision with effective numerical topology preservation.Significance: This framework challenges the traditional population-based learning paradigm, offering a highly flexible, robust, and promising solution for practical neuroimage analysis, particularly in clinical scenarios characterized by extreme data scarcity and complex cross-modality variations.

nodes.name: GDformer: Going Beyond Subsequence Isolation for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
nodes.venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
nodes.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection of multivariate time series is a challenging task, given the requirements of deriving a compact detection criterion without accessing the anomaly points. The existing methods are mainly based on reconstruction error or association divergence, which are both confined to isolated subsequences with limited horizons, hardly promising unified series-level criterion. In this paper, we propose the Global Dictionary-enhanced Transformer (GDformer) with a renovated dictionary-based cross attention mechanism to cultivate the global representations shared by all normal points in the entire series. Accordingly, the cross-attention maps reflect the correlation weights between the point and global representations, which naturally leads to the representation-wise similarity-based detection criterion. To foster more compact detection boundary, prototypes are introduced to capture the distribution of normal point-global correlation weights. GDformer consistently achieves state-of-the-art unsupervised anomaly detection performance on five real-world benchmark datasets. Further experiments validate the global dictionary has great transferability among various datasets.

nodes.name: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
Forest Digital Terrain Model from Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and GEDI L2A Using an Explainable Boosting Machine
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Accurate ground elevation beneath forest canopies is important for terrain and forest-structure analysis, yet satellite-based elevation data can be affected by canopy and terrain conditions, while spaceborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides ground elevations only at discrete locations. Here, the elevation offset between the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (CopDEM) and Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) L2A ground elevation was estimated using an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) with topographic, canopy-structure, and CopDEM-uncertainty predictors to generate continuous forest digital terrain models (DTMs) for two regions in the Republic of Korea. Validation against independent airborne LiDAR data showed root mean square errors (RMSEs) of the proposed DTM of 4.10 m in the central-western region and 3.67 m in the eastern region. In the EBM, the CopDEM height error mask (HEM), canopy cover, and aspect contributed most to the estimated offset, and the magnitude and direction of their contributions varied across canopy–terrain conditions and between regions. Residual bias increased with canopy height and became more negative on steep slopes, where RMSE also increased. These results show that the proposed approach can generate continuous forest DTMs while quantifying the contributions of the main predictors to the offset, their variation across environmental conditions, and the conditions under which residual errors increase.

nodes.name: Environmental Perception and Sensing Systems for Intelligent Control: Multi-sensor Fusion and Closed-Loop Control Methods
nodes.venue: Applied and Computational Engineering
nodes.abstract: This paper reviews how perception systems in intelligent systems evolve from single sensing to multi-source collaboration and then to participation in closed-loop control. Sensors such as vision, LiDAR, radar, and IMU differ in spatial coverage, accuracy, and environmental adaptability, making fusion necessary; time synchronization and spatial alignment are its prerequisites. Each of the data-level, feature-level and decision-level fusion is appropriate to certain tasks. Calibration of sensors, degradation detection, and fault detection in complex conditions guarantee long-term reliability, and machine learning enhances the extraction of information. Control decisions are becoming more and more driven by perception information via state feedback such that quadruped robots are using multi-IMU proprioception to drive MPC switching and connected vehicles are modulating intersection control by sharing perception. The computational latency of complex fusion algorithms can be reduced by model compression, edge computing and hierarchical information processing to reduce real-time pressure on the algorithm, architecture and scheduling levels. Overall, the deep integration of perception and control is both an inevitable technological trend and a key path toward higher autonomy and reliability in unstructured environments.

nodes.name: Dynamic Environmental Risk Identification for Historic Buildings Based on Multi-Source Sensing Digital Twins
nodes.venue: Applied and Computational Engineering
nodes.abstract: Buildings with heritage suffer from various disturbances like hygrothermal disturbances, moisture, vibration, and crack problems which cannot be easily identified from sensor readings independently. In this research, a multi-source sensing-based digital twin is developed for identifying environmental risks dynamically in a monitored two-story building made of bricks and timber structure. Variables such as temperature, relative humidity, wall moisture, vibration, crack displacement, and weather data outside are synchronized every five minutes and mapped into IFC-based Heritage Building Information Model in Unity. With the Temporal Fusion Transformer, a multivariate history with 24 time steps is taken into account, and normal, hygrothermal instability, moisture infiltration, vibration abnormalities, and crack displacement risk predictions are done. The architecture includes class weights, adaptive temporal consistency, and spatial regularization of components. With temporal testing, macro-F1 of 0.891±0.012, AUROC of 0.962±0.006, and mean warning delay of 6.7±1.1 min were obtained which is better than LSTM and XGBoost models with p<0.001. Removal of moisture sensors yielded maximum drop of macro-F1 to 0.847±0.014. Digital twin localization error was 0.43±0.17 m.

nodes.name: Digital twins for robot-assisted nuclear decommissioning: a review of perception, radiological mapping, and model interoperability, with the DORADO project as a case study
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Nuclear Engineering
nodes.abstract: Nuclear decommissioning increasingly relies on digital technologies to support characterisation, planning, monitoring, and decision-making in environments where access is limited by radiation, contamination, or other operational constraints. Digital twins provide a framework for integrating geometric, radiological, and operational information, while robotic systems acquire data and perform tasks with reduced human exposure. Although often treated separately, the two are coupled through a continuous exchange of information: robotic observations update the digital representation of the facility, and the twin provides the context for mission planning and execution. This review examines that coupling from the perspective of information representation and information flow. Based on a structured search of the peer-reviewed literature, standards, and public technical reports, it covers geometric and radiological sensing, radiation-field estimation, geometric and semantic representations and their interoperability, geometry for radiation-transport calculation, localisation, change detection, mission planning, and data governance. Comparative tables summarise sensing technologies, radiological instruments, exchange formats, localisation approaches, international programmes, and the evidence obtained in real facilities to date. A dedicated section synthesises uncertainty propagation and verification and validation requirements for safety-relevant use. The EURATOM DORADO project is then presented separately as a case study, showing how the requirements identified in the review are addressed in an ongoing engineering programme and distinguishing published results from implementation and ongoing development. The review concludes that the main barriers are not the performance of individual sensors or algorithms but interoperability, end-to-end uncertainty management, validation under representative radiological conditions, and long-term data governance, and that most current systems operate at the level of digital shadows rather than fully bidirectional digital twins.

nodes.name: Deterministic Edge Acquisition of Contextual, Multimodal Physiological Signals: A Bilateral-Ready Dual-Core IoT Biosensing Architecture for Ageing-Focused Research
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Sensor capability has outpaced the architectures available to integrate it: in near-body multimodal sensing, the binding constraint is no longer whether a variable can be measured, but whether a platform coordinates heterogeneous channels while preserving timing integrity, contextual interpretability, and extensibility. The gap is acute in ageing-focused research, which needs both side-specific comparison and heterogeneous sensing. We present the Deterministic Embedded Acquisition Platform Biosensing Hub (DeAP-BioHub), a dual-core STM32H755 architecture isolating acquisition from variable-latency subsystems by peripheral ownership. A real-time Cortex-M4 domain performs scheduled sensing, timestamping, and record creation, and a bare-metal Cortex-M7 domain carries telemetry, file-system logging, and operator interaction; the two share only a non-cacheable region and hardware semaphores, exchanging fixed 464-byte records with build-time offset assertions. With telemetry and logging active, the environmental channel held its nominal period at 1000.000 ms, at 1 ms timestamp resolution (SD 0.188 ms, n = 452), 96.5% exactly at nominal; the infrared channel’s 0.517% excess traced to that sensor’s own refresh cycle rather than the scheduler, and no storage-synchronization signature was detectable in the four sessions (combined Rayleigh test, p = 0.99). Contextual sensing shares that scheduling, record structure, and timestamp source rather than sitting in metadata: a fingertip registration was summarized descriptively by a first-order approach (τ = 154 s, R2 = 0.997), and a session reading flat on infrared alone stayed diagnosable from the environmental record. Ageing-focused research is the target application: this is laboratory verification of the acquisition substrate, not evaluation in older adults or clinical validation.

nodes.name: Cross-Environment WiFi CSI Gesture Recognition Using a Domain-Generalized Multi-Scale Attention Residual Network with Robust Feature Learning
nodes.abstract: Abstract WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) records changes in wireless signals induced by hand and body motions, providing a practical and contact-free method of gesture recognition. Changes in the environment, multipath propagation, and signal circumstances might affect CSI patterns, making it tough to achieve consistent detection across varied indoor situations. In this paper, we provide a framework for WiFi CSI gesture recognition that works in any environment by using a robust feature-learning Domain-Generalized Multi-Scale Attention Residual Network. Meaningful patterns linked with various movements are identified by the framework via the use of CSI amplitude fluctuations throughout time and subcarriers. A Stable Field Various resolutions of the gesture are captured using multi-scale convolution, and the network is trained to concentrate on the most important features with the aid of channel and spatial attention. Stable model training and successful feature learning are both supported by residual connections. Evaluating performance in both learned and unknown situations, the trials take five gesture classes into account. The validation and training results for a robust domain demonstrate consistent recognition performance and continuous convergence. A Stable Field The framework’s recognition accuracy in the unseen test environment is 86%, while in the two training domains they are 94% and 91%, respectively. The t-SNE image further highlights the substantial differences across the gesture classes, suggesting that the learnt characteristics maintain their uniqueness even when exposed to different environments. A Stable Field According to the ablation research, each component contributes to the overall improvement in accuracy; for example, using multi-scale convolution increased accuracy from 72% to 79%, channel/spatial attention increased accuracy to 82%, and the full framework improved accuracy to 86%. A Stable Field The findings show that the suggested method can reliably and robustly recognize gestures based on WiFi CSI even when the interior environment is constantly changing.

nodes.name: Constraint-Aware Multimodal Bin Grasping and Singulation in Cluttered Environments
nodes.venue: AI
nodes.abstract: Rigid container walls invalidate the open-workspace assumptions of tabletop manipulation, leaving three coupled gaps: unconstrained trajectories can be wall-unsafe, single-point grasp checks reject accessible offset positions, and occlusion-removal actions can ignore wall proximity. This paper treats bin wall geometry as a first-class constraint. A multimodal framework couples YOLO11 instance segmentation with a radial-basis-function support vector machine (SVM) and geometric rules to select among five modes—direct grasping, height-based grasping, two-dimensional singulation, and partial and full occlusion removal based on target visibility, relative height, grasp feasibility and wall proximity. Every trajectory passes a common wall-constraint validator before reaching the controller. Experiments used a UR5e with an overhead RGB-D camera. YOLOv11m-Segmentation model reached 0.992 box and 0.991 mask mAP@0.5 with an average inference time of 0.4350 ± 0.11 s. Task success was 100.0%, 93.3%, and 86.66% at low, medium, and high clutter (30 trials per condition). At high clutter, the ablation increased TSR from 66.66% for the single-point wall-unaware baseline to 83.33% with multi-point grasp selection and 86.66% with wall-aware singulation. The proposed system achieved a 90% Task Success Rate (TSR), compared with Target-Oriented VPG, which achieved 60% TSR, and GraspNet with bin-wall constraints, which achieved 40% TSR with 10 trials in a high-clutter environment. Across the 90 proposed-system trials, six task failures were observed, but none involved wall contact. Because container awareness sits in the planning layer rather than the end-effector, the method retrofits to installed cells using standard two-finger hardware.

nodes.name: Cognitive Cybersecurity via Bio-Inspired Intelligence: A Starling Flock Optimized Spiking Neural Network for Resilient Mobile Threat Detection
nodes.venue: Acta Technica Jaurinensis
nodes.abstract: Real-time threat detection is critical for guaranteeing mobility systems in cognitive environments to function with little disruption. Through monitoring user behavior, system logs, and network traffic, such systems depend on sophisticated analytics and machine learning. This paper presents a new Intrusion Detection System (IDS) architecture leveraging a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) as a classifier and the Starling Flock Optimization Algorithm (SFOA) as a feature selector on the NSL-KDD dataset. The main objective is to enhance the accuracy of classification while lowering feature dimensionality and computational cost for effective real-time detection. SFOA, stimulated by starling flock behavior, dynamically chooses best feature subsets with balance between relevance and redundancy. The SNN, in turn, simulates biological neurons and processes these best features by mapping them into temporal spike trains, employing event-driven processing and Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) for detailed pattern detection. Our developed model shows excellent performance with accuracy of 99.02%, precision of 98.9%, recall of 99.18%, and a 99.04% F1-score, outperforming SVM, Random Forest, CNN, LSTM, and Transformer models. Based on only 18 chosen features, the model has an extremely fast inference time of 2.3 ms, which is perfect for real-time usage. Comparatives also confirm SFOA is superior to PSO, GWO, ACO, and DE in terms of convergence rate and feature compactness. Ablation experiments validate that SFOA, spike encoding, and STDP learning are all essential to the model's performance, making this hybrid architecture a scalable and energy-efficient solution for sophisticated intrusion detection.

nodes.name: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
nodes.abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

nodes.name: CAMRA: Cross-Architecture Multimodal Reinforcement Learning with Federated Adaptation for IoT Malware Detection and Classification
nodes.venue: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
nodes.abstract: Abstract The domain of Internet of Things (IoT) has been rapidly developing, consequently expanding the attack surface for malware that exploits vulnerabilities across various hardware architectures and evades conventional static detection techniques. Past frameworks for IoT malware detection and classification often rely on a single data modality or are designed for a specific device architecture, which limits their ability to detect and classify malware in heterogeneous environments. This paper proposes CAMRA, a cross-architecture malware detection and classification framework that combines multimodal data, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and Federated Learning (FL). Using the CIC-YNU-IoT-MAL-26 dataset, CAMRA fuses network-level (PCAP), hardware-level (SAR), and system-level (STRACE) data streams through cross-modal attention across the ARM, MIPS, MIPSEL, and x86 architectures. A DRL controller adapts the per-class loss weights during training to address class imbalance, and federated learning adapts the centrally trained model across architecture-specific clients while keeping their raw data local. Over ten random seeds, CAMRA achieves a Macro-F1 of $$0.752 \pm 0.012$$ (accuracy $$98.4\%$$ ), and the federated model achieves $$0.741 \pm 0.008$$ (accuracy $$98.6\%$$ ), outperforming every single-modality model and standard baseline. Ablation and paired statistical tests show that the frequency-based class weights and the loss function are the main drivers of performance, with the DRL controller performing on par with fixed class weighting. In holdout experiments, malware from unseen architectures and from an unseen malware family is detected as malicious, while an unseen ARM architecture leads to false alarms on benign data.

nodes.name: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
Battery State of Health Early Prediction via a Generative Adversarial Network and a Hybrid Deep Learning Model
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Early prediction of the State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for battery manufacturing and management. However, battery aging is complex and nonlinear, and scarce early data challenges long-term prediction. To address this, a data-driven SOH prediction method based on transfer learning is proposed. As SOH degradation relates to various factors, an improved TimeGAN is first employed for data augmentation and style transfer to expand the training dataset. Additionally, a hybrid architecture, ATTCN-Mamba, integrating attention mechanisms, temporal convolutional networks, and state-space models, is constructed to improve prediction accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms traditional models in key metrics. Furthermore, with the TimeGAN-based transfer learning strategy, the model significantly enhances prediction accuracy and robustness even with substantially reduced target-domain data, with RMSE, MSE, and MAPE lower than those of the baselines without transfer learning. The method also demonstrates broad prospects for high-precision, full-life-cycle battery health management under edge-cloud architectures and cloud-based battery management systems.

nodes.name: Assessing Carbon Stock and Sequestration Capacity of Phragmites australis Using Integrated Destructive Sampling and Remote Sensing Approaches in Arid Environments
nodes.venue: Plants
nodes.abstract: Phragmites australis (common reed) delivers key ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, yet its carbon storage potential in hyper-arid environments remains insufficiently quantified. This study combines destructive sampling, laboratory carbon analysis, and satellite-derived vegetation indices to establish a rigorously validated baseline for aboveground biomass (AGB) and carbon stocks in a constructed wetland in Oman (n = 12 plots). Using leave-one-out cross-validation, this study tested whether biomass-prediction approaches commonly applied in wetland carbon research, namely height-based allometric equations and satellite vegetation indices, generalize beyond the data used to build them. The results show that the height-based equations achieve a near-perfect statistical fit by mathematical construction rather than genuine predictive validity, and that satellite vegetation indices require a larger, independent sample than used here to achieve validated accuracy; together, these findings establish a concrete, quantitative benchmark for sampling design and model validation in data-limited hyper-arid systems. The corrected destructive-sampling dataset places carbon stock at this site between 0.19 and 1.95 kg/m2, depending on the measurement method used. Together, these results support P. australis-dominated constructed wetlands as measurable, nature-based carbon reservoirs and chart a clear, evidence-based path toward reliable, remote sensing-based carbon monitoring across the Gulf Cooperation Council region and other water-stressed environments.

nodes.name: A near-real-time UAV-based computer vision framework for fire and smoke detection and localization using YOLO object detection and visible light communication
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
nodes.abstract: Introduction Early and reliable fire and smoke detection is essential for effective emergency monitoring, particularly in UAV-based environments characterized by variable illumination, changing object scales, and smoke-related visual disturbances. This study proposes a near-real-time UAV-based computer vision framework integrating YOLO-based object detection, geometric fire-source localization, and visible light communication (VLC). Methods A dataset of 4,200 manually annotated fire and smoke images was divided into training, validation, and test subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio. YOLOv10, YOLOv11, and YOLOv12 architectures were compared using Precision, Recall, mAP50, mAP50-95, inference time, and frames per second. Fire-source localization was modeled using camera-ray projection and ground-plane intersection based on UAV position and camera geometry. RF and VLC communication were evaluated through analytical modeling and simulation. Results YOLOv10l demonstrated a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, achieving Precision of 0.962, Recall of 0.968, mAP50 of 0.980, and mAP50-95 of 0.676. Under the modeled communication conditions, VLC-assisted transmission showed signal loss of 5–10%, compared with 15–25% for RF communication, with estimated latency below 40 ms. Simulated fire-source localization errors ranged from 0.5 to 1.2 m and decreased to 0.3–0.5 m under multi-view triangulation assumptions. Discussion The findings demonstrate the potential of integrating YOLO-based fire and smoke detection with geometric localization and VLC-assisted communication for near-real-time UAV monitoring. The detection experiments were conducted using workstation hardware, while communication and localization results were obtained through modeling and simulation. Further onboard UAV testing and independent validation are required to assess real-world performance and generalizability.
